repos.title: v0.0.26
repos.body:
HushTelegram v0.0.26 has 82 patches for Telegram 13.2.2, both the Google Play build (`org.telegram.messenger`, version code 73031) and telegram.org's (`org.telegram.messenger.web`, version code 73039). It moves to Morphe patcher 2.4.0, so update Morphe Manager to 2.6.0 or newer before you refresh the source. Nearly all of it came from your reports, and it changes something for #46, #65, #69, #71, #72, #73, #76, #77, #78, #79, #80, #82, #83, #85, #86, #87, #88, #89, #90, #91, #94 and #95. Call recording gets a record and pause button on the call screen, its own folder and a notification when a call's saved. Forwarding out of protected channels works now, the settings come in Simplified Chinese, and there's a long list of smaller switches from #79. Every new switch starts off.

New in this release

- `Save downloaded files` has a new switch, `File icons and thumbnails`, off by default. An APK or EXE sent as a file gets an Android-style or Windows-style icon of its own in Shared media's Files tab, and in the chat once it's downloaded. A downloaded PDF shows its first page in both places and a downloaded video a frame from it, made in the background. Files with a thumbnail from Telegram keep it, and anything not downloaded yet keeps Telegram's icon. (#79)

- `Disable draft link previews` has a new switch, `Fix link previews`, off by default. A link you send gets its preview from another site by the rules in `Link preview rules`, one rule per line, and the message keeps the link you typed. The rules start with posts on X, TikTok, Reddit and Instagram plus everything on pixiv. A rule can name a path, like `x.com/*/status -> fixupx.com`, with `*` for any one part, so a profile link keeps Telegram's own preview instead of the fixer site's page. Secret chats, edits and bot results keep Telegram's own preview. (#79)

- `Ask before sending a sticker` has two new questions, each with its own switch and each off by default. `Ask before sending a message` asks Send or Cancel when the send button or the keyboard's send key would send what you typed, and Cancel leaves the text, its reply and its link preview where they were. Scheduled and silent messages, edits and forwards still go out without asking. `Ask before joining a voice chat` asks Join or Cancel before you join a group's voice chat or a channel's live stream, and starting a new one doesn't ask. Round video messages also get their own switch, `Ask before sending a round video message`, apart from `Ask before sending a voice message`. If you had the old voice and video question on, both stay on. (#79)

- HushTelegram's settings come in Simplified Chinese. With Telegram or the phone set to Chinese (Simplified), every HushTelegram page, switch, dialog and message shows in Chinese. (#80)

- `Your own chat list title` is a new switch in Look and feel, under `Emoji next to the chat list title`, off by default. Type a name of up to 24 characters in `Text for the chat list title` and it shows at the top of the chat list in place of "Telegram", in the title's own bold font and theme color, after a restart. Leave the text empty to get Telegram's name back. It lives on this phone only and goes along with settings export and import. (#86)

- `Hide pinned message bar` is a new switch under `Hide translate bar`, off by default. It takes away the bar under a chat's top bar that shows pinned messages, with its counter and list button, and the chat moves up into the space. The messages stay pinned and nothing gets marked as read. Flip it with a chat open behind the settings and that chat's bar goes or comes back as soon as you're back in it. (#85)

- `Record calls` has three new rows under it. `Calls to record` picks every call, private calls only, voice chats and live streams only, or just the chats you pick. Pick those in `Chats to record`, or long press chats in the chat list and use `Record calls here` in the three dots menu. `Keep recordings` can delete recordings older than 7, 30 or 90 days each time a new one is saved, and it only ever touches the call recordings HushTelegram made. Recordings are named after the person or group now, like "Telegram call with Alex Kim 2026-11-12 14-05.m4a". (#72)

- While `Record button on calls` is recording, the button shows how long the recording runs and a pause button sits next to it. Whatever is said during a pause stays out of the file, and the call still saves as one recording. A tap on the record button records the call you're on even when `Calls to record` would skip it. (#72)

- `Notify when a call is saved` puts up a notification after each recording. Tap it to play the recording, or use its buttons to share it or send it straight to your Saved Messages. It's off until you turn it on, and it needs Android 10 or newer. (#72)

- `Save recordings as Opus` saves calls as .ogg files about half the size of the usual .m4a. It's there on Android 10 and newer, and a phone that can't write Opus keeps saving .m4a. (#72)

- `Recordings folder` lets you pick any folder on the phone for call recordings. Keep recordings cleans that folder too. If Telegram loses access to it, say after the folder's deleted, recordings go back to the usual folder until you pick another one. (#72)

- `Record button on calls` shows on voice chats and live streams too, at the start of the row of buttons in the top right corner. It records and pauses there the same way it does on a call. (#72)

- `Delete account` on the Privacy page deletes the account you're signed in with, right from the app. It asks first. When the account has a cloud password, Telegram waits a week before it deletes anything. (#71)

- `Show all spoilers and quotes`, under `Reveal spoilers`, adds two items to a chat's menu at the top. `Show all spoilers` uncovers every spoiler in the messages loaded so far, as if you'd tapped each one, and `Expand all quotes` opens every collapsed quote. View-once and sensitive media keep their blur. (#71)

- With `Open quotes on search hits` on, a chat search that lands on a match inside a collapsed quote opens the quote, so the match Telegram highlights is right there to see. (#71)

- `Select all` sits next to `Select between` under `Add Repeat to the message menu`, off by default. It puts a Select all button in the bar that shows while you pick messages, both in a chat and in a chat's shared media (photos, files, voice messages, links, music and GIFs). One tap selects everything loaded there, newest first, up to Telegram's 100 message limit. (#73)

- `Skip between voice messages` is a new switch under `Voice messages in the music player`, off by default. With it on, next and previous on headphones, in a car, in the notification, on the lock screen and in the full player move through a chat's voice messages the way they do through songs. Previous starts the message over when it's been playing for more than 3 seconds, and goes back one when it hasn't. Songs and view-once messages keep Telegram's own buttons. (#77)

- With `Read receipts button` on, every chat's menu at the top has a `Send read receipts` item too. It sends the read receipt Ghost mode is holding for that chat only, so one person sees you've read their messages and nobody else does. (#69)

- With `Read receipts button` on, a long press on a folder tab shows `Send read receipts` right under `Mark all as read`. While Ghost mode holds your reads, Mark all as read only clears the badges on this phone. This one sends them, so your other devices catch up. (#65)

- `Keep my messages too` sits under `Keep deleted messages`, off by default. When someone deletes a whole chat for both of you, your own messages stay along with theirs instead of only theirs. Messages you delete on another of your devices stay on this phone too. (#82)

- `Remove kept messages after` sits under `Clear kept messages`. Pick 1, 7, 30 or 90 days and a kept message goes away on its own that long after it was deleted, the same way Clear kept messages removes it. It's set to `Never` by default, so nothing changes until you pick. Messages kept before this update start counting after it, so none of them disappear the moment you pick. (#91)

- `Also save from secret chats` is a new switch under `Save downloaded files`, off by default. Together with `Also save from chats that don't allow saving`, files, photos and videos from secret chats get copied to Download/Telegram as well, and the message menu's `Save to Downloads` shows up there. Their view-once and timed media also need `Also save view-once and timed media`. (#82)

- `Also allow screenshots in secret chats` sits under `Allow screenshots in chats that don't allow saving`, off by default. With both on, screenshots and screen recording work in secret chats, their photos and their profiles. Telegram may still tell the other person when you take one. (#82)

- `Keep self-destructing secret chat messages` sits under `Keep deleted messages`, off by default. Messages, photos and videos in a secret chat stay on your phone when their self-destruct timer runs out. The other person's copy still goes on their own timer. (#82)

- With `Open restricted channels` on, the alert Telegram shows when a public channel has banned you gets an `Open on the web` button. It opens the channel's page at t.me/s/ in your browser, where its posts still show to anyone. The button shows only when HushTelegram knows the channel's public name, from the channel itself or from the link that brought you to it. (#71)

- `Keep chats you're removed from` sits under `Keep deleted messages`, off by default. When a group or channel removes or bans you, it stays in your chat list with the messages this phone already saved. Opening it shows a short note instead of Telegram's alert, and you can scroll back through it but not post. Delete it from the chat list when you're done and it's gone for good. Chats you leave yourself work as usual. (#71)

- `Message details` lists more about a file. You get its name and MIME type, the resolution of a photo or video, and the length and average bitrate of a song, voice message or video. Telegram doesn't send a bitrate, so it's worked out from the file's size and length. A line with nothing to show is left out. (#87)

- `Check Also delete for by default` is a new switch under `Add Repeat to the message menu`, off by default. With it on, the Also delete for box in Telegram's delete dialog starts checked, so messages you delete in a chat with a person go for both of you. Groups, channels, secret chats and Saved Messages don't change, since Telegram doesn't offer the box there. Uncheck it in the dialog to delete just for you. (#83)

- `Device in Active sessions`, on the Privacy page under `Don't notify contacts`, sets the device name and system version your other phones and computers see for this one in Settings > Devices. Leave a box empty and Telegram's own goes out. A change shows after you restart Telegram. (#79)

- With `Ghost mode` keeping read receipts back, a long press on a message someone sent you offers `Send read receipt`. They see that message, and the ones before it, as read, while Ghost mode stays on for everything else. It works in chats with people, groups and supergroups. Channels already send their reads, and secret chats aren't covered. (#79)

- `Show when an account was made` is a new switch under `Show user and chat IDs`, off by default. A person's profile menu then shows about which month they joined Telegram, such as "Registered about March 2016", right under the ID row. The month is worked out on the phone from the user ID and a table of IDs with publicly known sign-up dates, so it's an estimate and nothing is asked of Telegram. An account newer than the table reads "Registered after" its last month. Bots, groups and channels get no row, and tapping the row copies it. (#79)

- `Show when members joined` is a new switch under `Show user and chat IDs`, off by default. A group's member list on its profile and its Members page then add when each person joined to the line under their name, such as "last seen recently · joined 12 Mar 2024, 14:05", written the way your phone writes dates. The date already comes with the list, so nothing more is asked of Telegram. Admins and the owner keep their role there, and a member Telegram sends no date for shows nothing extra. (#79)

- `Show when forwards were first sent` is a new switch under `Show user and chat IDs`, off by default. A forwarded message's header then adds when the original was sent, such as "Forwarded from · 12 Mar 2024, 14:05", written the way your phone writes dates. In compact chats the date goes after the sender's name in the one-line header. The date already comes with the message, so nothing more is asked of Telegram, and messages that aren't forwards look the same as before. (#79)

- `Pin chats on this phone` is a new switch on the Chat list page under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. A long press in the chat list then offers `Pin on this phone` in the three dots menu, and `Unpin on this phone` once every chat you picked is pinned that way. Those chats sit right under Telegram's own pinned chats in All Chats, newest message first, up to 20 of them. Nothing goes to Telegram, so the pin limit, your server pins and your other devices stay as they are. The archive and the folder tabs keep Telegram's order, and the list goes along in a settings file. (#79)

- `Change avatar size` is a new switch on the Chat list page under `Hide folder tab counters`, off by default. Chat pictures in the chat list show at the size you pick in `Avatar size` right below it, from 70% to 120% of Telegram's. Every row keeps its height and its text, and the picture stays centered in its spot, with the story ring, online dot and rounded corners following it. Turning it on or picking another size changes the chats already on screen right away. The size goes along in a settings file. (#89)

- `Hide Contacts tab` has one more switch on the Chat list page, `Outline the bottom bar`, off by default. It draws a thin line in Telegram blue around the bar at the bottom of the main screen, so the bar stands out on AMOLED black and other dark themes. Telegram's other glass panels keep their look. Restart Telegram after flipping it. (#90)

- `Do Not Disturb in the chat list menu` is a new switch on the Chat list page under `Proxy in the chat list menu`, off by default. The menu at the top of the chat list then ends with `Turn on Do Not Disturb`, and one tap there silences every message notification until you tap `Turn off Do Not Disturb`. A short toast says which way it went. While it's on, nothing new shows, sounds or vibrates for private chats, groups, channels, mentions or bots, and a message coming into the chat you have open makes no sound either. Messages still arrive and unread counts still go up. Calls ring as usual. Turning it off, or pausing HushTelegram, brings Telegram's notifications back with the next message, and a settings file never carries whether it's on. (#79)

- `Picture behind the lists` is a new switch on the Look and feel page under `AMOLED black`, off by default. Pick a photo in `Background picture` and it shows behind the chat list, Settings, profiles, contacts, calls and the other list pages, with the rows see-through over it. You choose how dim it is, from 20 to 80 percent. Chats keep their own wallpaper, and menus, dialogs, sheets, the keyboard panel and the media viewer stay solid. The photo is copied into Telegram's own files, so it stays after a restart or an account switch, and `Remove background` puts Telegram's look back right away. It works with Telegram's built-in themes and needs Android 13 or newer, so older phones don't show the two rows. A settings file carries the switch and the dim but not the photo. (#88)

- `Chat list banner` is a new choice on the Look and feel page under `Your own chat list title`, off by default. Pick one of five color pairs (Dusk, Ocean, Forest, Ember or Slate) or a photo from your gallery, and the bar at the top of the chat list shows it. The colors switch with a light or dark theme so the title and icons stay easy to read, and a photo sits under a light veil for the same reason. Only the chat list's own bar changes. Folder tabs and the bar shrinking as you scroll work as before, and `None` puts Telegram's bar back right away. A settings file carries the choice but not the photo. (#86)

- `Add Bookmark to the message menu` is a new switch under `Add Repeat to the message menu` on the Conversations page, off by default. Long press any message, post, photo, video or file and tap `Bookmark` to keep a note of it on this phone. While it's saved the item reads `Remove bookmark`. The `Bookmarks` page, right below the switch and in the chat list's side menu, lists them newest first with the chat's name, a short preview and the date. Tap one and its chat opens at that message, highlighted the way a reply jump does it, and a long press or the Remove button takes it off the list. If the message is gone or you've left the chat, it tells you. The list keeps up to 100 bookmarks, nothing goes to Telegram, and settings export and import carry them, adding a file's bookmarks to the ones already on the phone. (#79)

- `Use system font` can now draw all of Telegram's text in a font file of your own. Tap `Font file`, right under the switch, and pick a .ttf or .otf file from your phone. Picking one turns `Use system font` on, and the font shows after a restart. Most fonts come with one weight, so bold text is that font drawn thicker. Code blocks keep a monospace face, and Telegram's digit and Instant View faces stay as they are. Tap the row again to choose another font or remove it. The file stays on this phone and isn't part of settings export. (#79)

- `Admin tools` is a new switch under `My messages` on the Conversations page, off by default. A group or channel you own or manage then has `Admin tools` in its menu at the top. It lists Recent Actions, Administrators, Members (Subscribers in a channel), Permissions or Removed Users, and Invite Links, as far as your rights there go, and each one opens Telegram's own screen. (#79)

- `Admin folder` is a new switch under `Folders by chat type` on the Chat list page, off by default. Turning it on makes an ordinary Telegram folder called Admin with every group and channel you own or manage, so it's a tab above your chats here and on your other devices. While it's on, the folder keeps up as you gain or lose rights somewhere, about once a minute at most. Turning it off removes the folder, unless you renamed it or changed what's in it. (#79)

- `Voice changer` is a new choice on the Playback page, under `Play voice messages one at a time`, and it starts off. Pick Baby, Woman, Man, Horror movie or Robot, and the voice messages you record come out in that voice, waveform and all. It covers both of Telegram's voice recorders, and a recording keeps the voice it started with. (#79)

- `Add Edit a copy to the message menu` is a new switch under `Add Repeat to the message menu` on the Conversations page, off by default. Long press a photo that's on your phone and tap `Edit a copy` to open it in Telegram's own photo editor, where you can draw on it or blur the parts you don't want to share. Sending from the editor posts the edited copy to the same chat, and the photo you started from stays as it was. It only shows in chats you can send to that also allow forwarding. (#79)

- `Audio track and subtitles` is a new switch under `Start videos without sound` on the Playback page, off by default. A video's settings menu, the one with Loop video, then offers `Audio track` when the video has more than one, and `Subtitles` when it has any. Pick a track and the video switches to it, and the list keeps it ticked even after the video loops. Subtitles show as lines near the bottom of the video, and `Off` hides them again. A video with one audio track and no subtitles keeps Telegram's menu as it is. (#79)

- `Recognize files you already have` is a new switch under Save downloaded files on the Playback page, off by default. A file, photo or video Telegram already downloaded, in another account for example, shows as downloaded and opens right away when Telegram's folders hold one with the same name and size. Telegram's servers don't send a fingerprint of a file, so name and size are what it goes by, the same check Telegram makes itself when you tap download. With `Keep Telegram's files in internal storage` on, files from before a reinstall count too. (#79)

Fixes

- With `Ask before sending a round video message` on, Cancel keeps the video you just recorded in the chat bar, paused, so you can still send it or delete it. The question used to come up only after Telegram had let go of the recording, which left an empty bar. Sending from a locked recording's send button asks too, and a clip too short for Telegram to keep no longer gets a question. (#79)

- A suggestion card in Settings, like "Is this still your number?", goes away as soon as you answer it. Telegram 13.2's new Settings page listened for those changes in a place Telegram never sends them, so the card stayed until you left Settings and came back. Changes to your name or photo show there right away now too. (#76)

- With `Hide phone number` on, the "Is this still your number?" card shows your real number, since you can't answer it about a row of dots. Your profile and the rest of Settings keep it covered. (#76)

- Turning `Hide phone number` on or off changes the number at the top of Settings and on the Profile tab right away. Telegram 13.2 keeps its Settings tab built, so the number up there kept its old look until Telegram restarted.

- With `Bypass channel restrictions` on, a forward out of a channel or chat that turns forwarding off now arrives. Telegram's servers turn those forwards down whatever the app says, so HushTelegram sends each message again as a new one instead, its text or its photo, video or file with the caption. They go out as your own messages, without the "Forwarded from" line. A video or file that isn't on the phone yet downloads first. Auto-forwarding rules that watch a protected chat go the same way. (#73, #94, #95)

- Files now go out with `Forward as copy` and with a forward out of a protected chat. Telegram won't send a file from the app's private storage, which is where the renamed copy was made, so a PDF or any other document stopped at "Unsupported attachment". The copy now sits in the app's cache on shared storage, next to Telegram's own downloads. (#46, #94)

- With `Bypass channel restrictions` on, Forward, Copy, Save to Gallery and the Share button show up on protected messages and work. That goes for the bar you get while picking messages, the message menu, shared media and the photo viewer. The switch only answered Telegram's chat-wide check before. Each protected message carries its own lock too, and a few screens read the channel's lock straight off the channel, so Forward on a post from a protected channel or a message a bot protected did nothing and Copy and Save stayed hidden. Stars, brackets, emoji or text right after a link no longer lose it, and neither does a server name ending in a dot or a secret written in standard base64. A list served as one block of base64 is decoded first. On a public list of 420 links that used to lose 58 of them, only the 8 with a broken port or a cut-off secret get skipped. `Find free proxies now` also says how many proxies were read, as in "10 of 406 read". They stay covered and in the original language, where the plain-text translation used to show them uncovered.

- The German "Couldn't save that. Try again." toast is shorter and fits in two lines on a small phone. It used to run onto a third.

Other changes

- Both builds move from Telegram 13.2.1 to 13.2.2, code 73031 from Google Play and 73039 from telegram.org.

- HushTelegram now builds on Morphe patcher 2.4.0, the one in Morphe Manager 2.6.0 and morphe-desktop 2.2.0. Manager won't load a bundle made with a newer patcher than its own, so update Manager to 2.6.0 or newer before you add this release.

Behind the scenes

- Release publish reads the notes GitHub serves back as UTF-8, so a bullet with an accented word like "Português" no longer looks missing after the release is already up.

The [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) has every earlier release too.

How to update

1. Install [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.6.0 or newer. Older Managers won't load this bundle, since it's built on Morphe patcher 2.4.0.
2. Add HushTelegram as a patch source: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushTelegram. If you already have it, refresh the source. Morphe Manager shows it as signed by d7d6 bd99 8faf 7bcc.
3. Get Telegram 13.2.2. From Google Play that's `org.telegram.messenger` with version code 73031, which [APKMirror](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/telegram-fz-llc/telegram/) carries too. telegram.org's build is `org.telegram.messenger.web` with version code 73039, from the [Download button](https://telegram.org/android). Once telegram.org moves past 13.2.2, Telegram's own [Telegram APKs for Android](https://t.me/TAndroidAPK) channel still has this one. The patched app needs Android 9 or newer.
4. Coming from 0.0.25? Patch 13.2.2 and install it over your current HushTelegram with the same Morphe Manager signing key. Your settings and chats stay. New to HushTelegram? Uninstall the stock Telegram first, since Android won't put a patched app over one signed with a different key. Your chats come back when you sign in, but secret chats don't. Back up Morphe Manager's signing key after your first patch. You'll need it for every update.
5. If Telegram turns down your login code with `API_ID_PUBLISHED_FLOOD`, it's refusing the public API ID that ships with any patched build. Register your own app at [my.telegram.org/apps](https://my.telegram.org/apps), using only letters and numbers in the short name. Then select `Use registered Telegram API credentials`, fill in `apiId` and `apiHash`, and patch again. Keep both values private.
6. Want HushTelegram's own icon, or Telegram's logo in white on the black launch screen? Turn on Expert mode in Morphe Manager and pick `HushTelegram icon and name` or `Black and white launch logo` before you patch.
7. To change HushTelegram's switches, open Telegram's Settings and tap HushTelegram settings, or press and hold the Telegram title at the top of your chat list.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Telegram APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTelegram#install).

What was checked

All 2802 runtime tests passed locally, and all 742 patch tests passed too (166 unit tests and 576 that patch the real Telegram APKs), along with both Android lints (the shared library and the Telegram extension). Every one of the 82 patches applied without forcing to telegram.org's Telegram 13.2.2 (version code 73039) and to the Google Play build of 13.2.2 (version code 73031). For each patched build the release receipt checked the package name, version, manifest, resource table, native libraries and zip alignment.

Both patched builds were installed over a signed-in copy on an Android 13 emulator, keeping its data, and each one walked through 22 screens without a crash. Android's own code verifier (dex2oat) raised nothing on either build, same as on unpatched Telegram.

hushthreads.title: v0.0.18
hushthreads.body:
HushThreads v0.0.18 has 26 patches for Threads 455.0.0.55.72 (`com.instagram.barcelona`), and it patches that version only, on all nine APKMirror variants. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.3.0, so you need Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer. Update Threads to 455 before you patch.

Four new patches. `Spoof SIM region` lets Threads see a SIM from a country you pick, and `Full size profile pictures` opens someone's profile picture in a viewer of its own. `Change package name` and `Change app name` put HushThreads next to your regular Threads as a second app. The suggested threads under a post you open can go now too.

**Your reports in this release**

- [#8](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/8) found that Meta's own Instagram won't open Threads posts in HushThreads. The note under Links in HushThreads settings points to the way round it now, which is patching Instagram with HushGram in the same Morphe Manager.
- [#22](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/22) asked to see a profile picture full size. `Full size profile pictures` opens it in its own viewer with pinch to zoom, and with Save media on there's a Save button too.
- [#23](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/23) asked for a way to keep the regular Threads and have HushThreads beside it. `Change package name` and `Change app name` do that, and the copy has its own sign-in.
- [#24](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/24) asked to hide the suggested threads under a post's replies. `Hide suggested threads` on the Feed page takes them away, and it starts on.
- [#25](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/25) asked to change the region Threads sees. Turn on `Spoof SIM region` under Privacy and pick a country, and Threads reads that country's SIM and carrier instead of yours.

## Threads

- Meta's own Instagram won't open Threads posts in HushThreads, and the note about it under Links in HushThreads settings now tells you what to do instead. Patch Instagram with HushGram in the same Morphe Manager so both share one key, and Instagram opens Threads posts and profiles right in HushThreads. Asked about in #8.
- New `Spoof SIM region` patch. Threads sees a SIM and network from the country you pick, with one of that country's real carriers, instead of your own. There are 69 countries to choose from. It starts off, so turn it on and pick one in HushThreads settings > Privacy. Meta can still go by your connection and your account, so it won't hide where you are by itself. Asked for in #25.
- HushThreads now patches Threads 455.0.0.55.72 only, on all nine APKMirror variants (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and x86). Update Threads to 455 before you patch. v0.0.17 is the last release for 454.0.0.54.79.
- Hide ads and Hide suggested users keep up with how Threads 455 stores For You. It writes every page and every single post straight into the feed cache now, and it can slip an ad into a page you're already scrolling. All of those go through the filters, and a page keeps its posts as they were when an ad gets turned away.
- Hide suggested users also takes the suggested threads off the bottom of a post you open. It has its own switch, `Hide suggested threads`, under the other two on the Feed page, and it starts on. The post and its replies stay. Asked for in #24.
- New `Full size profile pictures` patch. When you open someone's profile picture on their profile, it shows full size in a viewer of its own instead of Threads' small circle. You can pinch to zoom, and with Save media on there's a Save button too. It's in Manager's default selection, but its switch under Appearance in HushThreads settings starts off. Asked for in #22.
- The bundle is built on Morphe patcher 2.3.0 now, the one that comes with Morphe Manager 2.5.0 and Morphe Desktop 2.1.0. Older Manager builds can't load it, so update Manager to 2.5.0 or newer first.
- With `Show exact post times` on and a large font, a post's time stays in one piece. Under a long name it used to break after the month or the day, with "Nov" on one line and "5, 2:30 AM" on the next. Now the whole time moves under the name when it doesn't fit beside it.
- New `Change package name` and `Change app name` patches. Keep your regular Threads and install HushThreads next to it as a second app with its own sign-in. Neither patch is in Manager's default selection. HushThreads settings show the copy's package name and app name under Set when you patched. Asked for in #23.

## Tooling

- The full patch check, which applies every patch, passes with `Change package name` in the bundle. It used to read the renamed package and its renamed permissions as an unknown app asking for new permissions. The checks that compare a patched build with the clean one follow Threads 455 too, where three of the places they read had moved.

## Update

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.5.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.18 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Get Threads 455.0.0.55.72 for your phone (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 or x86) and patch that. v0.0.17 was the last release for Threads 454.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change package name`, `Change app name`, `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first, or patch with `Change package name` to keep both.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).

## Validation

1106 runtime tests and 346 patch tests passed locally, along with both Android lints and the release script checks. All 26 patches applied without forcing to Threads 455.0.0.55.72, and the release receipt records the run. The dependency advisory check passed.

1. You need [Morphe Manager](https://github.com/MorpheApp/morphe-manager) 2.5.0 or newer. If HushThreads is already one of your patch sources, Manager shows 0.0.18 once it refreshes. If it isn't, add it: https://morphe.software/add-source?github=SysAdminDoc%2FHushThreads
2. Get Threads 455.0.0.55.72 for your phone (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 or x86) and patch that. v0.0.17 was the last release for Threads 454.
3. Manager's default selection has every patch except `Change package name`, `Change app name`, `Change version code`, `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates`. Turn on Expert mode if you want any of those.
4. Patch with the Morphe Manager signing key you used last time. That's what lets the update install over your patched Threads and keep your data and your login. Coming from the stock Threads, uninstall it first, or patch with `Change package name` to keep both.
5. On a fresh install, sign in with your Instagram username and password.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Threads APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads#install).
